cs.label: [section] Cíl předmětu a studijní výstupy:
cs.content: Cílem předmětu je seznámit posluchače s metodami a technikami studia vývoje a aktuálního stavu krajiny. Hlavní důraz je kladen na postupy hodnocení a diagnostiky krajiny, určování jejího potenciálu a limitů a budování informačního systému o území. V předmětu je kladen důraz na analýzu, syntézu a evaluaci krajinného systému. Posluchači se seznámí s postupy průzkumů a rozborů pro potřeby krajinného plánu. Významnou část semestru tvoří legislativní základ územního plánování.

Landscape -- interpretation of the concept from the point of view of planning. Recapitulation of landscape-ecological connections. Definition and interpretation of basic concepts (potential, carrying capacity, suitability of the landscape). Landscape versus territorial planning -- basic starting points and principles.The course is based on present European and Czech legislation and international conventions (i.e. building act, EIA act, ESPOO convention etc.). Principles of functional and spatial structure of a territory, limits of a territorial land use, buffer zones designing, typology and placing of buildings are characterised. Urbanisation and rural settlements are understood in their agroecological and sociological aspects. The following important factors of territorial planning are described: natural, industrial, agricultural, transport, defence, demographic, sociological and cultural. Territorial systems of ecological stability are understood as the basis of landscape planning. EIA is mainly orientated on farm animal stables, processing of agricultural products and foodstuffs production. In a seminar students prepare a simple land-use plan of a territory including territorial system of ecological stability. EIA of a selected activity includes multicriterial analysis of identified impacts. (allowance 2/2)

Landscape structure. Natural and socio-economic factors. Landscape dynamics and approaches to its investigation.International context of landscape planning. European Landscape Convention. Landscape typology. (allowance 2/2)
Methods of landscape planning. From LANDEP to spatial difference methods. (allowance 2/2)
Content and standards of landscape ecological plan. Preventive landscape protection. Conflict management in the territory. SWOT analysis. Problem map. (allowance 2/2)
EIA and SEA process. Principles, process, and content of documentation. (allowance 2/2)
Perception and aesthetics of the landscape and its importance in spatial planning. Mental maps. Landscape assessment. (allowance 2/2)
Assessment of landscape character - principles and methods. Historical landscape structures. Evaluation of changes in the development of landscape structure. (allowance 2/2)

Spatial planning materials and spatial planning documentation (SPD). The content of the documentation and the process of entering, processing, and approving the SPD. Surveys and analyses of the territory. (allowance 2/2)

Spatial planning in the Czech Republic, comparison with other countries. Objectives, tasks, and tools of spatial planning. Territorial planning authorities, the process of territorial planning in terms of state administration. (allowance 2/2)
Master plan in detail. (allowance 2/2)
Current problems of the landscape (fragmentation, suburbanization, brownfields). Tools and management. (allowance 2/2)
The relationship between territorial and strategic planning. (allowance 2/2)

en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The aim of the course is to familiarize students with methods and techniques of development and current state of the landscape at a particular time and space. The main emphasis is placed on evaluation and diagnosis of the landscape, identifying its potential and limits, and building a territory information system. The course emphasis is placed on analysis, synthesis and evaluation of the landscape. Students will learn research methods and practices for the needs of the landscape plan.

en.content: 1.Landscape -- interpretation of the concept from the point of view of planning. Recapitulation of landscape-ecological connections. Definition and interpretation of basic concepts (potential, carrying capacity, suitability of the landscape). Landscape versus territorial planning -- basic starting points and principles.The course is based on present European and Czech legislation and international conventions (i.e. building act, EIA act, ESPOO convention etc.). Principles of functional and spatial structure of a territory, limits of a territorial land use, buffer zones designing, typology and placing of buildings are characterised. Urbanisation and rural settlements are understood in their agroecological and sociological aspects. The following important factors of territorial planning are described: natural, industrial, agricultural, transport, defence, demographic, sociological and cultural. Territorial systems of ecological stability are understood as the basis of landscape planning. EIA is mainly orientated on farm animal stables, processing of agricultural products and foodstuffs production. In a seminar students prepare a simple land-use plan of a territory including territorial system of ecological stability. EIA of a selected activity includes multicriterial analysis of identified impacts. (allowance 2/2)2.Landscape structure. Natural and socio-economic factors. From LANDEP to spatial difference methods. (allowance 2/2)4.Content and standards of landscape ecological plan. Preventive landscape protection. Conflict management in the territory. SWOT analysis. (allowance 2/2)6.Perception and aesthetics of the landscape and its importance in spatial planning. Mental maps. Landscape assessment. (allowance 2/2)7.Assessment of landscape character - principles and methods. Historical landscape structures. Evaluation of changes in the development of landscape structure. (allowance 2/2)8.Spatial planning materials and spatial planning documentation (SPD). The content of the documentation and the process of entering, processing, and approving the SPD. Surveys and analyses of the territory. (allowance 2/2)9.Spatial planning in the Czech Republic, comparison with other countries. Objectives, tasks, and tools of spatial planning. Territorial planning authorities, the process of territorial planning in terms of state administration. (allowance 2/2)10.Master plan in detail. (allowance 2/2)11.Current problems of the landscape (fragmentation, suburbanization, brownfields). Tools and management. (allowance 2/2)12.The relationship between territorial and strategic planning. en.label: [section] Assessment methods:
en.content: Obligatory participation in seminars (up to three pre-excused absences) One 60-minute written test (at least 75 % to receive credit). Participation in the test is compulsory (at the end of the course -- 12th week). Fulfilled test is compulsory for final exam participation. A field trip is a mandatory part of the course. Preparation and submission of seminar projects. Seminar work is submitted in the 11th week. The course is finished with an oral exam (length of about 25 min). (5 credits)
